name: Iona

text: Iona is a Scottish mythological site. It is now best known as the center of Celtic Christianity founded by Saint Columcille. The tiny island sits in Scotland's Inner Hebrides. A Celtic shrine to a goddess once stood there. The goddess Ioua gave the island its first name. She has been read as a moon divinity. Others connect the name to a word for yew, a tree of sacred places and death. The island's holy well rose from the magic cauldron of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Its name, Tobar na h'oige, means fountain of youth. Those who looked into the well at dusk, at dawn, or on the night of the full moon saw visions and received healing. As a Celtic site it admitted both men and women. Under Christianity women, except nuns, could not live there. One of the island's churches keeps a figure called a Sheela Na Gig. She is a pregnant woman shown exposing herself.
